blocks.html: Why understanding matters, but why some of the deepest layers of healing ask us to listen beyond the mind.

We have become very good at understanding ourselves. We know about childhood patterns, attachment styles, trauma, triggers and the nervous system. We can trace our reactions back to experiences that shaped us and develop an extraordinary amount of insight into why we think, feel and behave as we do.

Understanding matters. It can bring awareness, compassion and choice. It can help us recognise patterns that were previously invisible and give us language for experiences that were difficult to understand. But what if we have come to rely on the mind a little too heavily in the process of healing?

What if we believe that we need to understand exactly what happened, where it came from and why we carry it before we can release it? There are experiences we can explain perfectly and still carry. We can know why we become anxious and still feel the anxiety. We can understand our childhood and still carry an emotional response from it. We can recognise a relationship pattern and still feel energetically connected to the person or experience.
Understanding and release are not always the same thing.
The Limits Of The Mind

Our minds are extraordinarily powerful, but they operate within a particular structure. The mind experiences our lives through memory, language, perception and the linear passage of time. It wants to categorise, understand, connect cause and effect and create a coherent story. These capacities are invaluable, but they may not be the only way we experience ourselves.

If we understand ourselves as multidimensional energy beings, then the mind is one way of experiencing who we are, rather than the entirety of who we are. Our energetic and spiritual experience may extend beyond the linear framework through which the mind understands our lives. This opens another possibility in healing: perhaps we do not have to understand everything before we can begin to release it.

There may be experiences, patterns and imprints held within us that the conscious mind cannot yet see. Rather than asking the mind to solve everything, we can become curious about what is already present and allow another kind of knowing to emerge.
The question changes from “What is wrong with me, and why is this happening?” to “What does my energy field want to reveal?” And then: “What is ready to be released?”
Allowing The Field To Reveal The Story
blocks.text: Allowing The Field To Reveal The Story

blocks.html: This is something that can become particularly apparent in energy healing. A person may arrive believing they know exactly what they need to work on. They may have spent years understanding a particular relationship, childhood experience or emotional pattern and may already have a clear explanation for why they feel the way they do.

Sometimes that understanding reveals something important. But sometimes the deeper work begins when we stop trying to make the mind solve the experience and instead create space to listen to what the energy is holding. We can ask what is ready to be seen, what is ready to move and what is ready to be released, without deciding beforehand what the answer should be.

One layer may reveal another. An experience that appears to be about the present may lead towards childhood. A childhood pattern may reveal a family or ancestral thread. Within a spiritual or shamanic context, what emerges may be understood through karmic or past-life experience. The origin may turn out to be somewhere completely different from where we thought we needed to look.

The important thing is not to force the experience into a predetermined explanation. We can remain curious about what it is revealing, what meaning it holds and what is ready to change. The healing does not always depend on having a perfect explanation. Sometimes the revelation itself creates an opening.
When The Story Goes Deeper

There are times when what emerges seems to reach beyond our personal biography. A recurring pattern may appear to have an ancestral quality. A relationship may carry a sense of familiarity that is difficult to explain through present circumstances alone. A person may experience imagery, sensations or a sense of knowing that they understand through a karmic or past-life lens.

These experiences invite us to consider a possibility that can feel unfamiliar to the rational mind: that not everything we carry necessarily begins with the life we consciously remember. Within spiritual traditions, ancestral patterns, karmic imprints and past-life experiences are understood as possible layers of human experience. They offer another way of exploring why certain themes, emotions or relationships may feel unusually persistent or charged.

We do not need to decide in advance that this must be the explanation. The value can be in remaining open enough to explore what arises and discerning what meaning it holds. Sometimes what first appears to be a personal pattern reveals an ancestral thread. Sometimes the experience opens a question about karma or another lifetime. Sometimes it leads somewhere entirely unexpected.
The point is not to replace one fixed story with another. It is to allow the possibility that the story may be larger than the mind initially imagined.
The Value Of Not Knowing

Perhaps there is a form of intelligence in healing that we do not talk about enough: the intelligence of not knowing. Not ignorance, not avoidance and not bypassing, but the willingness to say, “I don't know yet.” I don't know where this came from. I don't know why this keeps happening. I don't know what is being held here.

Instead of rushing to fill that space with an explanation, we can become curious. We can listen to the body, the breath and the energy. We can become attentive to what emerges through sound, emotion, sensation, imagery, intuition or spiritual practice. We can ask, “What does my energy field want to reveal?” and “What is ready to be released?”

Perhaps what emerges confirms what we already knew. Perhaps it reveals something completely different. Perhaps one layer leads to another, and a story that initially appeared to be about the present reveals a much older pattern. The point is not to force an answer. It is to create enough openness for something deeper to become known.

That openness is important. Healing can become another exercise in control when we decide in advance what must be found, how it must be understood and what the outcome should be. Sometimes we need to soften our grip on the need to know and allow the process to show us something we could not have arrived at through thought alone.
Allowing The Energy Field To Reveal
blocks.text: Allowing The Energy Field To Reveal

blocks.html: Different forms of energy healing can provide different ways of entering this territory. The intention is not to decide that one approach is better than another, but to recognise that people can respond to different forms of experience and that different doorways may be appropriate at different points in a person's journey.

Reiki can offer a gentle space for stillness, relaxation and connection with subtle energetic experience. Shamanic Energy Healing can explore energetic, ancestral and soul-level dimensions, including soul retrieval where appropriate. Therapeutic Sound Healing works through sound, vibration, resonance and deep listening, offering another way of experiencing what is held beyond ordinary verbal processing.

Womb Healing offers women a particular space to explore embodied, emotional, energetic and symbolic experiences connected with the womb and the feminine. Breathwork can bring attention directly into the body and breath, while hypnotherapy can provide a doorway into subconscious patterns and beliefs. Ayurveda brings another perspective through the relationship between lifestyle, wellbeing and balance.

These approaches do not need to compete with one another. They are different languages and different ways of meeting the human experience. The question is not which modality is the most powerful, but what is appropriate for this person, at this time, and what is ready to be explored.
Opening The Mind To A Pattern Beyond This Lifetime
blocks.text: Opening The Mind To A Pattern Beyond This Lifetime

blocks.html: Vedic Astrology offers yet another lens through which a person can explore the possibility that some of the patterns they are experiencing have a karmic dimension. Within the Vedic tradition, the birth chart is not simply viewed as a description of personality. It can be read as a symbolic map of tendencies, cycles, challenges and themes that unfold through a lifetime.

From this perspective, certain recurring experiences may invite a different question. Rather than only asking, “Why did this happen to me?” we can ask, “What pattern is being presented here, and what might I be learning through it?” The language of karma can offer a way of considering patterns that seem to extend beyond the immediate circumstances of our lives and, within a spiritual worldview, may be connected with experiences beyond this lifetime.

This does not require us to turn every difficulty into a karmic explanation. Nor does it mean that a chart determines our destiny. Used thoughtfully, Vedic Astrology can be a reflective tool — another perspective that can illuminate themes, timing and possibilities that may not be obvious from our immediate experience.

It can also remind us that the mind's story about who we are is not necessarily the whole story. Sometimes a pattern becomes easier to understand when we step back from the individual event and see it as part of a larger cycle. And sometimes that broader perspective creates the space to choose differently.
When There Is Space For The Story To Unravel
blocks.text: When There Is Space For The Story To Unravel

blocks.html: Sometimes this work needs more than an individual session. It needs space. A 1:1 transformational retreat creates an opportunity to step outside the familiar environments, responsibilities and distractions that can keep us moving through life on autopilot. It creates time to slow down, listen and become more aware of what is actually happening within us.

Importantly, the work does not have to be completely mapped out before it begins. One layer can reveal another. The energy field can begin to unravel a story, and as one layer is understood or released, something deeper may become accessible. What initially appears to be about one experience can reveal a much older pattern. What seems psychological can open into the body. What feels personal can reveal an ancestral thread. What appears emotional can lead somewhere spiritual.

A personalised retreat allows there to be time to follow that unfolding. The intention is not to force someone through every modality or decide in advance what needs to happen. It is to create a sufficiently held and personalised space in which the work can respond to what is emerging. One day may call for deep rest and reflection; another may involve breathwork, sound, Reiki, shamanic exploration, Womb Healing, Ayurvedic practices, Vedic Astrology or simply time to integrate.

The value is in having enough time to listen before deciding what comes next. The journey can unfold progressively, with each layer informing the next, rather than requiring the entire process to be understood at the beginning.
We do not have to know the whole journey before we begin walking it. We can meet what is ready when it arrives.
Understanding Is Part Of The Journey
blocks.text: Understanding Is Part Of The Journey

blocks.html: There is no need to reject the mind. Understanding is valuable. It helps us make sense of our experiences, integrate what we discover and make conscious choices about our lives. The invitation is simply to release the idea that everything must first make sense to the mind before it can change.

If we are more than our thoughts, memories and personal stories, then perhaps there are other ways of knowing available to us. The body can reveal. The breath can reveal. The energy can reveal. Sound can reveal. The subconscious can reveal. Spiritual practice can reveal. A symbolic system such as Vedic Astrology can offer another perspective.

Sometimes we need to understand the story. Sometimes we need to move beyond the story. Sometimes the mind leads, sometimes the body speaks, sometimes emotion reveals, and sometimes energy opens another doorway. Healing does not have to be linear, and it does not have to be explained in advance.

So perhaps the question is not simply, “What do I need to understand so that I can heal?” Perhaps it is, “What does my energy field want to reveal, and what is it ready to release?” And perhaps the deeper question still is, “Can I allow myself to be open to the possibility that the answer may be somewhere my mind has never thought to look?”

Because some healing can be understood. Some healing needs to be felt. Some healing needs to be moved. Some healing needs to be released. And some healing may take us somewhere far beyond the story we thought we came to heal.
We do not always need to think our way through it. Sometimes we need to become still enough to listen, and open enough to let the deeper layers reveal themselves.
Our personalised 1:1 transformational retreats and one-to-one healing sessions create space to slow down, listen deeply and explore what is ready to be understood, experienced and released.
You don't have to know everything before you begin. You simply need to be open to discovering what is waiting to be revealed.

blocks.html: What source consciousness reveals
During a recent shamanic energy healing session, a single word entered the healing field with remarkable clarity:
Mirth.

Almost immediately, the energetic landscape began to reorganise. The field expanded, strengthened and became palpably lighter. The session was no longer centred solely on releasing old patterns. Instead, it began rewiring consciousness around an entirely different organising principle—the transformative power of joy.
So why mirth?
Why would Source Consciousness choose a word so often associated with laughter and amusement to guide a profound healing experience?

Much of modern spirituality has come to associate transformation with effort, discipline and suffering. Many seekers believe awakening requires endless shadow work, continual self-improvement and the relentless dismantling of old identities. While each has its place, they represent only one movement within a far greater unfolding.

Creation itself reveals another way.  The natural world does not strive to become what it already is. A flower does not force itself to bloom. Birds do not earn the right to sing. Rivers do not struggle towards the ocean. Life unfolds through an innate intelligence expressed as rhythm, creativity, curiosity and joyful expansion.

We too are designed to align with this natural unfolding.This is where the deeper symbolism of mirth emerges. Mirth is not merely happiness, because happiness often depends upon circumstance. Nor is it pleasure that comes and goes, or excitement that fades once the moment has passed. Mirth is something far more fundamental.  It is the quiet delight of existence itself.

The simple, uncaused joy of being alive.  There are moments when we unexpectedly remember this state. Standing before a magnificent sunrise. Listening to birdsong at dawn. Feeling the warmth of sunlight upon our skin. Walking barefoot on the earth. Watching a child laugh without restraint. For a brief moment, nothing needs to change. Nothing needs to be achieved. We simply become present to the extraordinary miracle of existence. This is our original nature.

It is not something we create, but something we remember. As we remember it, our energy field naturally begins to reorganise around it. Joy is no longer dependent upon external circumstances. Instead, it arises from the exquisite privilege of simply being alive.
As the healing continued, it became increasingly clear that the invitation was not simply to feel happier.  The healing field was reorganising consciousness around this deeper remembrance.

It gently loosened the patterns that had organised life around striving, survival and perpetual self-improvement, while strengthening a new orientation founded upon presence, play, wonder and wholehearted participation in life itself.  From this perspective, healing changes completely.

Healing is no longer only about releasing the past.  It becomes the remembrance of what has always existed beneath it.  Joy is no longer the reward waiting at the end of the healing journey.It becomes the stable ground from which the journey itself unfolds.

The invitation of Mirth is beautifully simple.  Do not wait for life to become perfect before allowing yourself to experience its wonder.  Do not postpone joy.Instead, create moments to consciously return to the simple delight of being alive.

This does not mean bypassing life's challenges. Rather, it is the recognition that beneath every circumstance exists a deeper frequency that remains untouched. A frequency we can consciously choose to align with, regardless of what life is asking of us.  Sometimes this remembrance comes effortlessly.
At other times it asks us to slow down, become still, and gently reconnect with what has never truly been lost. The more often we remember this state, the more naturally it becomes available.
Perhaps the deepest healing is not found in changing our circumstances, but in remembering that the greatest miracle was never what life could give us.  It was life itself.
The journey revealed the symbol. Source Consciousness revealed the teaching.

blocks.html: ‍‍What Source Consciousness Reveals

During a recent shamanic energy healing session, a spiral shell emerged within the journey. It arrived quietly, without explanation or instruction. Like many symbols that arise during healing, it simply presented itself, inviting a deeper question. Why this image? Why now? More importantly, why has the spiral shell appeared throughout nature, ancient cultures and spiritual traditions for thousands of years?
Perhaps the more meaningful question is not what the spiral shell meant in one particular journey, but what Source Consciousness continually reveals through this timeless symbol.

The spiral is one of the oldest sacred patterns found in creation. It is woven into galaxies, hurricanes, seashells, unfurling ferns, fingerprints and even the delicate architecture of the inner ear. Nature returns to the spiral again and again because it is far more than a beautiful form. It is an architecture of growth.

Unlike a straight line that moves from one point to another, the spiral teaches that evolution is cyclical. We revisit familiar experiences, yet never from exactly the same place. Each return carries greater awareness, deeper wisdom and a broader perspective than before.

This understanding quietly challenges one of the greatest misconceptions about healing. Many people believe that once a lesson has been learned it should never return. Yet those who walk a genuine path of transformation know that healing is rarely linear. We often encounter the same themes repeatedly, not because we have failed, but because consciousness is inviting us to meet them from a more expanded state of being. The spiral reminds us that repetition is not regression. It is evolution.

The shell itself carries another profound teaching. It is both sanctuary and home. Unlike armour, which is put on for protection, a shell grows from within. It expands naturally as the life it shelters expands. Protection, therefore, is not something acquired from the outside world. It is something cultivated through the gradual expansion of consciousness.

There comes a point on every spiritual path where safety is no longer found through certainty, control or external validation. It is discovered by becoming deeply established within one's own centre. The shell reminds us that our greatest refuge is not somewhere we find, but someone we become.

For those engaged in profound healing, this symbolism is especially significant. The journey is not about becoming someone new. It is about growing into a fuller expression of who we have always been. Like the chambers of the shell, every experience, every initiation and every season of life becomes part of the architecture of the soul. Nothing is wasted. Everything contributes to our expansion.

The spiral shell also speaks to the wisdom of the Divine Feminine. Throughout history, the feminine has understood creation not as something forced into existence, but as something allowed to unfold according to its own innate intelligence. The womb itself embodies this principle. Life does not emerge through striving. It develops through rhythm, nourishment and sacred timing. The spiral reflects this same movement. It teaches us that the deepest transformations rarely occur through force. They emerge through trust, presence and allowing.

Perhaps this is why symbols such as the spiral shell appear so consistently within healing journeys. Source Consciousness does not always communicate through language. Sometimes it communicates through symbols that speak directly to the deeper intelligence of the soul. A single image can convey what pages of explanation cannot. Symbols bypass the analytical mind and awaken a remembering that already exists within us.

The invitation of the spiral shell is beautifully simple. Stop measuring your life by how far you have travelled away from your past. Instead, notice how much more deeply you inhabit your own centre each time life brings you full circle. What once appeared to be repetition may, in truth, be evidence of expansion.
The journey revealed the symbol.
Source Consciousness revealed the teaching.
Healing is not a straight path towards perfection. It is the graceful spiral through which consciousness continually returns to itself, each time remembering a little more of what it has always been.

blocks.html: ‍When women first encounter the idea of the Womb Guardian, they often imagine that she exists only within healing ceremonies or moments of deep meditation. In my experience as a shamanic practitioner, however, the Guardian is never confined to sacred space. She walks beside us into relationships, motherhood, business, creativity, leadership and every place where our life force is asked to meet the world. Her influence is subtle enough that we rarely recognise it. Instead, we assume our protective habits are simply our personality. Yet beneath many recurring patterns lives an intelligent, devoted protector whose purpose has always been to safeguard the deepest parts of us.

The Womb Guardian is not an obstacle to overcome. She is a sophisticated survival intelligence. She remembers what the mind has forgotten, stores experiences that shaped our sense of safety, and quietly evaluates every situation through one simple question: 'Is it safe to open?' When life has contained betrayal, criticism, abandonment, shame or disappointment, the Guardian adapts. Those adaptations are rarely mistakes. They are expressions of love attempting to protect what feels most precious.

This understanding invites a profound shift. Rather than asking, 'Why am I like this?', we begin asking, 'What has my Guardian been trying to protect?' That single question moves us from self-judgement to self-compassion. Instead of fighting ourselves, we begin listening. In that listening, healing becomes possible.
The Guardian in Relationships

Relationships often reveal the Guardian most clearly because intimacy requires vulnerability. Some Guardians protect by keeping people at a distance, attracting emotionally unavailable partners or withdrawing before closeness develops. Others protect through over-giving, rescuing, people pleasing and becoming indispensable in the hope that love will remain. Although these behaviours appear opposite, both arise from the same longing for safety. As genuine experiences of trust accumulate, the Guardian slowly learns that love no longer needs to be survived; it can simply be received.
The Guardian in Motherhood

Whether expressed through biological children, mentoring, teaching or caring for others, motherhood awakens the Guardian's protective instincts. Healthy protection creates secure boundaries and emotional safety. Unresolved protection, however, can become overprotection, anxiety or chronic self-sacrifice. One of the greatest gifts we can offer the next generation is not perfection but a regulated nervous system. When we learn to return to calm, we teach resilience without speaking a word.
The Guardian in Leadership ‍

Many women believe they must become harder to lead effectively. Yet authentic feminine leadership arises from regulated presence rather than force. If visibility once led to criticism or rejection, the Guardian may encourage perfectionism, undercharging or remaining invisible. Healing allows leadership to emerge from grounded confidence instead of fear, making room for wisdom, compassion and clear boundaries.
The Guardian and Sexuality

The womb has long symbolised creation, intimacy and relational connection. When trust has been broken, the Guardian naturally becomes more vigilant. Healing is never about forcing openness. It begins by restoring choice, consent, agency and safety. Only then does the body remember that intimacy can once again be nourishing rather than threatening.
The Guardian in Business ‍

Our businesses often mirror our nervous system. Fear of visibility, difficulty receiving money, burnout, overworking and weak boundaries frequently reflect a Guardian trying to keep us safe. A sovereign business honours both generosity and sustainability. Healthy boundaries are not a withdrawal of love; they are one of its most mature expressions.
The Guardian and Creativity

Every act of creativity asks us to reveal something personal. Creative blocks are not always a lack of inspiration; sometimes they are acts of protection. As the Guardian experiences greater inner safety, expression becomes more natural and creativity begins to flow with less effort.
The Guardian and the Mother Line
blocks.text: The Guardian and the Mother Line

blocks.html: We inherit more than physical characteristics from our ancestors. We inherit beliefs about love, money, motherhood, visibility and safety. Within many shamanic traditions, ancestral healing is not about blame but remembrance. We honour the women who came before us while consciously choosing which patterns continue through us and which conclude with us.
The Guardian's Greatest Desire

At her core, the Guardian does not seek control. She seeks confidence that you can now meet life consciously. She longs to exchange hypervigilance for discernment, fear for intuition, control for trust and survival for sovereignty. She has faithfully guarded the doorway to your inner temple, waiting not to dominate your life but to walk beside you as a wise ally.
Embodiment Practice

Sit comfortably with one hand over your heart and the other over your lower abdomen. Breathe slowly. Bring to mind an area of your life where tension repeatedly appears. Ask gently: What is my Guardian protecting? Where do I feel this in my body? What would help this part of me feel just one percent safer today? Resist the urge to analyse. Simply listen.
Journal Reflections

items: Where does my Guardian appear most strongly in my life?
Which protective patterns have genuinely served me?
Which patterns now limit the life I long to create?
What would discernment look like instead of hypervigilance?
Which beliefs may have been inherited rather than consciously chosen?
If my Guardian trusted that I could protect myself today, how might my life change?

blocks.html: Walking the Path of Sovereignty

Recognising the Womb Guardian is not about eliminating your protective instincts. It is about transforming them. The Guardian has carried your story with extraordinary devotion. When she is finally met with compassion instead of resistance, protection begins to soften into wisdom. That is the beginning of sovereignty—not because the Guardian disappears, but because she no longer needs to stand alone.
You can learn more about an individual Womb Healing Session here:
Womb Healing at The Juicy Effect

If, after experiencing this work, you feel called into a deeper process of remembrance and transformation, you may also wish to explore Womb Alchemy: A Return to Sovereignty—an immersive journey that unfolds over several months through embodiment practices, shamanic healing, ceremony, reflection, and integration.
This path isn't about fixing yourself.
It is about remembering the wisdom, power, and sovereignty that have always lived within you—waiting patiently beneath every layer of protection.

Within Womb Alchemy: A Return to Sovereignty, we explore this relationship experientially through guided shamanic journeying, embodiment practices, nervous system awareness, energy healing and reflective inquiry. Rather than analysing the Guardian from a distance, you are invited into a living relationship with her—one that gradually transforms protection into discernment and survival into embodied sovereignty.
The deepest healing does not come from fighting the Guardian.
It comes from thanking her for everything she has carried, and gently showing her that she no longer has to carry it alone.

blocks.html: "There comes a moment on every healing journey when we realise that the very thing preventing us from opening our hearts was never our enemy. It was our protector."
Many women come to healing believing there is something wrong with them.

They wonder why they cannot fully trust. Why intimacy feels frightening. Why they overthink every decision. Why they continually attract unavailable partners. Why they struggle to receive support. Why they find themselves exhausted from always being the strong one.

From the outside, these behaviours can appear contradictory. A woman may be deeply compassionate yet fiercely guarded. She may long for connection while instinctively pushing people away. She may crave rest while feeling unable to stop doing.
Within shamanic practice, there is another way of understanding these patterns.

Rather than seeing these responses as flaws, many traditions view them as the work of an inner protector—an archetypal intelligence whose role is to preserve the sanctity of the deepest parts of ourselves. Within the framework of my work, I call this presence the Womb Guardian.

The Womb Guardian is not something that needs to be believed in as a literal being. Instead, she can be understood as an archetypal protector encountered through deep meditation, shamanic journeying, ceremony, dream work, or profound inner reflection. Some women experience her as a wise elder. Others as a warrior. Others encounter an animal, a serpent, a great tree, an ancient queen, or even a solid stone wall. Each encounter is deeply personal, yet the underlying purpose remains remarkably consistent.
She protects.
Not because she wishes to keep love out.
But because somewhere along the way, love stopped feeling safe.
Looking Through Three Lenses
Throughout this article, I invite you to explore the Womb Guardian through three complementary perspectives.
The Shamanic Lens

In many indigenous and shamanic traditions, healing involves entering an altered state of consciousness to meet symbolic guides, ancestors, power animals, or aspects of ourselves that hold wisdom. The Womb Guardian belongs to this symbolic landscape. She represents an inner intelligence that regulates access to our deepest feminine centre.
The Psychological Lens

Modern psychology offers a different but complementary understanding. Following painful experiences, our minds naturally develop protective adaptations. We become cautious, hyper-independent, perfectionistic, people-pleasing, emotionally numb, or endlessly productive. These strategies are not signs of weakness—they are evidence of the human nervous system doing its best to keep us safe.

Many therapeutic approaches describe these adaptations as protective "parts" that formed in response to overwhelming experiences. While different models use different language, they share a common understanding: protection develops for a reason.
The Nervous System Lens

Neuroscience has also transformed our understanding of healing. Our nervous system continually assesses whether our environment feels safe or threatening. This process happens largely outside conscious awareness and influences everything from muscle tension and digestion to emotional regulation, connection, and decision-making.

Although some popular theories about the nervous system continue to be debated within scientific literature, there is broad agreement that repeated experiences shape our physiological responses over time. Chronic stress, trauma, and unpredictable environments can leave the body primed for protection, while repeated experiences of safety, supportive relationships, and gentle regulation can gradually expand our capacity to feel secure again.
From this perspective, the Womb Guardian can also be understood as the lived expression of a nervous system that has learned to protect what is precious.
These three lenses are not competing explanations.
They simply offer different languages describing the same human experience.
The Original Role of the Guardian
blocks.text: The Original Role of the Guardian

blocks.html: I do not believe the Womb Guardian was created by trauma.  I believe she existed long before it.

In her original form, the Guardian is discerning rather than fearful.  She knows when to open and when to close.  She recognises genuine safety without becoming naïve.  She honours intuition without becoming suspicious of everyone.  She protects life force without imprisoning it.

Imagine the entrance to an ancient temple.  Not everyone is invited inside.  Those who enter do so with respect, humility, and clear intention.  No one would call the guardian standing at the entrance "closed-hearted."
She simply understands that sacred spaces deserve discernment.

The womb—whether understood biologically, energetically, or symbolically—is one of those sacred spaces.  It is a centre of creation.  A place where life, ideas, relationships, purpose, and identity are continually conceived and nurtured.  The Guardian's original purpose is not to prevent life from entering.
Her purpose is to ensure that only what truly nourishes life is welcomed.
When Protection Becomes Survival

Problems arise when the Guardian is asked to carry more than she was ever designed to hold.  A child who grows up feeling emotionally unsafe may learn that vulnerability is dangerous.  A woman who repeatedly experiences betrayal may conclude that trust is naïve.  Years of criticism may teach the body that visibility leads to rejection.
Grief may teach the heart that attachment inevitably ends in loss.

None of these conclusions are conscious choices.  They are intelligent adaptations.  The nervous system remembers what the mind has long forgotten.  Eventually, the Guardian begins responding not only to genuine danger, but also to reminders of previous pain.
This is where discernment quietly transforms into hypervigilance.
Boundaries become walls.
Wisdom becomes control.
Protection becomes isolation.
The Guardian is no longer protecting the temple.
She is living inside a permanent state of emergency.
The Guardian Is Not Your Enemy
blocks.text: The Guardian Is Not Your Enemy

blocks.html: One of the greatest mistakes we can make on a healing journey is trying to destroy the very parts of ourselves that once ensured our survival.
Many women speak about wanting to "break down their walls."  I would suggest something gentler.
Rather than demolishing the walls, perhaps we first walk alongside them. Perhaps we ask: "What happened that made these walls feel necessary?"
Healing rarely begins with force.  It begins with curiosity.

Every protective response deserves compassion before it is invited to transform.   The Guardian does not soften because she is told to.  She softens because, often for the first time, she genuinely experiences safety.  And safety cannot be rushed.
It is cultivated.
One regulated breath.
One honest conversation.
One nourishing relationship.
One embodied moment at a time.
A Gentle Embodiment Practice: Meeting Your Guardian
blocks.text: A Gentle Embodiment Practice: Meeting Your Guardian

blocks.html: Find a quiet place where you will not be disturbed for ten to fifteen minutes.
Sit comfortably with both feet on the floor or lie down with one hand resting over your heart and the other over your lower abdomen.
Take several slow breaths, allowing your exhale to become a little longer than your inhale.
Notice the support beneath your body.
Notice the temperature of the room.
Allow your attention to settle into the present moment.
Now, gently ask yourself: "If the part of me that has been protecting my deepest self could take a form today, what would it look like?"
Do not force an answer.  Simply notice.
Perhaps an image arises.
Perhaps a sensation.
Perhaps only a feeling.
Without trying to change anything, silently ask:

items: How long have you carried this role?
What do you most want me to understand?
What helps you feel safe enough to soften?
What do you need from me today?

blocks.html: There is no right or wrong experience.  The practice is not about creating a vivid vision.  It is about beginning a relationship with the parts of yourself that have been quietly working on your behalf all along.
Journal Reflections
After your practice, spend time reflecting on the following questions:

items: When do I feel most guarded?
What situations cause my body to tense before my mind understands why?
Which protective strategies have genuinely served me?
Which ones am I beginning to outgrow?
What does safety actually feel like in my body?
If my Guardian could speak with complete honesty, what would she most want me to hear?
What would trusting myself one percent more look like this week?

blocks.html: There is no need to answer perfectly.
Allow your responses to emerge with honesty rather than judgment.
The Journey Continues
Meeting the Womb Guardian is not about bypassing pain or dismantling your defences overnight.
It is about honouring the wisdom that has carried you this far while gently inviting a new possibility.

Over time, the Guardian begins to remember that her deepest role is not simply protection—it is discernment, devotion, and the safeguarding of your creative life force. As the nervous system experiences greater moments of genuine safety, many women find that trust becomes less of an effort and more of an embodied experience.
This meeting is often the first threshold.
Beyond it lie deeper layers of remembrance: the Inner Queen, the Sacred Descent, ancestral healing, embodied sovereignty, and the reclamation of the feminine wisdom that has always lived within you.

These themes form the heart of Womb Alchemy: A Return to Sovereignty, where this work unfolds through guided embodiment practices, shamanic journeying, energy healing, reflection, and integration. The intention is not simply to understand these concepts intellectually, but to experience them in a way that supports lasting transformation.
Perhaps the greatest gift of the Womb Guardian is this gentle reminder:
The parts of you that have been protecting your heart are not standing in the way of your healing.
They are waiting to walk beside you as you remember who you have always been.

It rises from somewhere much deeper, feeling less like learning something new and more like remembering something ancient.

Many women describe this moment as a subtle awareness that, despite success or outward fulfilment, something essential has been forgotten. They have spent years caring for others, striving, producing and achieving, yet feel increasingly disconnected from themselves. The journey that follows is not about becoming someone new. It is about returning home.

Across many wisdom traditions the womb has been honoured as more than a physical organ. It represents creativity, intuition, life force and deep inner knowing. Whether understood spiritually, symbolically or through embodied experience, reconnecting with this inner centre can profoundly change the way a woman relates to herself and to life.
This article is an invitation to explore sovereignty not as domination or control, but as a deeply embodied relationship with yourself.
The Path Back to Yourself

Sovereignty begins with self-relationship. It is the ability to hear your own inner truth even when the world is speaking loudly. It is saying yes because your heart is aligned and saying no because your body knows a boundary is needed.

Many women notice that healing first appears in the body. Their breath naturally deepens. Their jaw softens. The shoulders slowly release. The constant gripping through the belly or pelvis begins to ease. Instead of feeling as though they are forcing life forward, they begin to experience moments of being carried by life.

Rather than seeing these changes as goals to achieve, they can be understood as signs that the nervous system is beginning to experience greater safety. When the body no longer feels it must remain on constant alert, intuition has room to emerge.
The Sacred Descent
Modern culture celebrates ascent—more success, more speed, more productivity. The feminine often invites the opposite. She invites descent.

The sacred descent is not about withdrawing from life. It is about moving beneath the noise of the thinking mind into a quieter place where wisdom already exists. It is choosing presence over performance.

This descent often happens through ordinary moments: taking a conscious breath, resting without guilt, walking in nature without needing to achieve anything, or noticing the quiet voice of intuition before the louder voice of fear. These moments gradually reshape a woman's relationship with herself.
Meeting the Womb Guardian
Every sacred space has a guardian. In my work I describe this as the Womb Guardian—the part of us that learned to protect vulnerability, creativity and innocence.
Sometimes the Guardian appears strong and fiercely protective. Sometimes she feels distant, cautious or hidden. Whatever form she takes, she developed for a reason.

Women often experience her presence through the body before recognising her consciously. Tightness around the hips, tension through the pelvic bowl, holding the breath or withdrawing from intimacy may all reflect protective patterns. They are not signs of failure. They are invitations to meet ourselves with compassion.
Healing is rarely about forcing openness. It is about creating enough inner safety that the body no longer needs to remain defended.
Awakening the Inner Queen
Beyond protection waits another archetype: the Inner Queen.
The Inner Queen does not dominate. She leads through presence, integrity and self-respect. She knows her worth without demanding validation.

As women embody this aspect of themselves they often describe subtle yet profound changes. Their voice becomes steadier. Their posture naturally lengthens. Decisions are made with less hesitation. Relationships become healthier because self-abandonment is no longer mistaken for love.
Embodied sovereignty is often quiet. It is found in calm choices rather than dramatic declarations.

The body frequently reflects this shift. Breathing feels easier. The heart softens. There is less urgency to control outcomes and more willingness to participate in life with openness.
Living Sovereignty
Sovereignty is not the destination; it is a way of living.

It means choosing authenticity over approval. It means allowing your intuition to guide your decisions. It means recognising that your creativity, boundaries and sensitivity are strengths rather than weaknesses.

As this way of living deepens, women often notice increased resilience, clearer relationships, renewed creativity and a greater capacity for joy. They stop asking who they should become and begin expressing who they have always been.
Healing does not erase every challenge. Instead, it changes the place from which we meet life's challenges.

blocks.html: One of the themes that often arises during Shamanic Energy Healing sessions is the desire to surrender, let go, and trust life more deeply. Clients frequently tell me that they want to stop fighting life. They want to trust the unfolding. They want to feel guided rather than controlled by fear. They want to move through uncertainty with greater peace and confidence.

To me, this is one of the great mastery journeys of being human. Not because life becomes easier, but because we learn to meet life differently. We learn to soften our grip. We learn to release the illusion that we can control every outcome. We learn to trust ourselves, trust our soul, and trust the deeper intelligence moving through life.

When a client expresses this desire, I know they are being called into a fuller expression of who they came here to be. Because becoming more of who we truly are requires a degree of surrender. It requires releasing old identities. It requires stepping beyond certainty. It requires saying yes to life even when we cannot see the entire path ahead.
Rather than asking yourself, "Do I trust life?" try asking a different question: How would trust feel in my body?

Pause for a moment. Take a breath. Imagine that everything currently unfolding in your life was being held within a larger intelligence. The joyful parts. The beautiful parts. The challenging parts. The heartbreaking parts. The uncertain parts. The parts that make no sense at all.
What would it feel like if your body met all of it with a deep and trusting yes?

Not necessarily approval. Not necessarily liking what is happening. But an openness to life as it is.  Would your shoulders soften? Would your breath deepen? Would your heart open? Would your nervous system relax? Would there be more spaciousness within you?
Trust is not simply a thought. Trust is an embodied experience. It is something we feel. And often the body reveals where trust has not yet been established.

Many people believe they should trust more. Yet beneath the surface may live experiences that taught them otherwise. Past disappointments. Betrayals. Loss. Unresolved grief. Childhood conditioning. Ancestral patterns. Generational survival strategies. Deep unconscious beliefs.

From a shamanic perspective, we can also explore karmic imprints, soul contracts, energetic entanglements, and inherited patterns that influence how we move through life. These layers often operate beneath conscious awareness. They shape our choices. They influence our relationships. They affect our ability to receive. And they can limit our capacity to trust the flow of life itself.

In a Shamanic Energy Healing session we are not attempting to force surrender. We are creating a space where the barriers to surrender can begin to reveal themselves. The unconscious patterns. The inherited beliefs. The ancestral imprints. The energetic attachments. The outdated survival mechanisms. The parts of you that still believe it is safer to control than to trust.
When these layers begin to emerge into awareness, they can be witnessed, understood, and gradually unravelled.

This is why healing is often a journey rather than a single event. Each layer that softens creates access to a deeper level of trust. Each session invites you into a greater degree of surrender that is appropriate for your life, your nervous system, and your soul's current stage of evolution.

One of the reasons I love this work is that it continually reminds me how multidimensional we truly are. We are more than our thoughts. More than our stories. More than our current circumstances. Within each person exists a vast landscape of experiences, wisdom, gifts, memories, and possibilities waiting to be explored.
Every healing session reveals another layer. Another doorway. Another opportunity for remembrance. Another invitation into greater wholeness.
The healing journey is not about becoming someone else. It is about uncovering more of who you have always been.
Take a moment and place your hand on your heart. Ask yourself: "If I trusted life just 5% more than I do right now, how would that feel in my body?"

Notice what changes. Notice what softens. Notice what opens. Allow yourself to experience that feeling, even for a few moments.  Because every journey into trust begins with a single yes.  And perhaps that yes is not to a future outcome.  Perhaps it is simply a yes to this moment.
A yes to your healing.
A yes to your unfolding.
A yes to life itself.

blocks.html: ‍One of the most common wounds that emerges during Inner Child Healing and Hypnotherapy sessions is the wound of not feeling seen. ‍Clients often arrive saying: "I feel invisible." "I feel overlooked." "I feel like nobody sees my value." "I give so much, but nobody appreciates me."

At first glance, it appears to be a problem with other people. The assumption is that if only others could recognise our gifts, appreciate our efforts, or acknowledge our worth, then the pain would disappear.
But healing often invites a deeper question:
If you do not feel seen by others, how are you not seeing yourself?
The Original Wound
As children, we develop our sense of self through our relationships with caregivers.

Healthy emotional development requires more than food, shelter, and physical care. A child also needs emotional attunement. They need someone to notice them, celebrate their uniqueness, reflect back their gifts, acknowledge their feelings, and witness their inner world.
When this happens consistently, a child learns: "I matter." "My feelings matter." "My needs matter." "I am valuable."
But when emotional attunement is absent, a different message can be absorbed: "My feelings don't matter." "I need to earn love." "I am not important." "I am invisible."

This wound is often subtle. There may have been no abuse. No dramatic trauma. Perhaps your parents loved you deeply. Yet they may have been emotionally unavailable, overwhelmed, distracted, stressed, or carrying unresolved wounds of their own.
The result is that nobody fully mirrored your essence back to you. Nobody truly saw you.
How the Wound Appears in Adulthood
blocks.text: How the Wound Appears in Adulthood

blocks.html: The child who was not seen often becomes the adult who desperately seeks recognition.

We may chase validation through achievement, relationships, service, people-pleasing, over-giving, or constantly proving our worth.  ‍Yet no amount of external recognition ever feels like enough.  ‍Because the wound is not actually about being seen by others.

The wound is that we learned not to see ourselves.  ‍Many people spend years waiting for someone else to finally provide the validation they never received as a child. A partner. A parent. A boss. A client. A friend.
But healing begins when we stop waiting.
Learning to See Yourself
The first stage of healing is awareness.
Can you begin to notice your gifts?
Can you acknowledge your strengths?
Can you recognise the qualities that make you unique?
Can you appreciate yourself without needing somebody else to confirm your value?

This is not arrogance. It is self-recognition. It is reclaiming the reflection that was missing.   ‍Many people can list their flaws instantly but struggle to name their gifts. That in itself reveals where the work begins.

One of the invitations of Inner Child Healing is to consciously begin seeing yourself in the way you longed to be seen by others. To acknowledge your kindness, your courage, your wisdom, your creativity, your resilience, and your heart.
The more you cultivate self-recognition, the less dependent you become on external validation.
Why Some People Don't Recognise Your Value
blocks.text: Why Some People Don't Recognise Your Value

blocks.html: There is another important truth.
Not everybody will recognise your gifts. And that does not mean your gifts are not valuable.   ‍People tend to value qualities they have cultivated within themselves.  ‍
Someone who values integrity will notice integrity.
Someone who values depth will appreciate depth.
Someone who values honesty will recognise honesty.
Someone who values compassion will notice compassion.

But a person who has never developed these qualities may overlook them completely.  ‍If one of your greatest gifts is integrity, a person who does not value integrity may never recognise it.   ‍If one of your gifts is emotional depth, someone uncomfortable with emotions may never appreciate it.   ‍If one of your gifts is authenticity, those invested in maintaining masks may find it confronting rather than inspiring.
This is not a reflection of your worth.  ‍It is a reflection of their perception.

The mistake many people make is allowing another person's inability to see them become evidence that they are not valuable.  ‍Your value does not increase when somebody recognises it, nor does it decrease when they fail to.
Healing the Unseen Child
This is where Inner Child Healing and Hypnotherapy can be profoundly transformative.  The unconscious mind often carries younger parts that still believe:
"I'm invisible."
"I'm not important."
"I don't matter."
"No one sees me."

These beliefs are rarely logical. They are emotional imprints formed during significant moments in childhood.  ‍Through gentle hypnotherapy and inner child work, these younger aspects can finally receive what they needed all along.
To be witnessed.
To be heard.
To be valued.
To be loved.
To be accepted exactly as they are.

As these parts begin to heal, something profound happens.  ‍The need for external validation starts to soften.  ‍You stop searching for proof of your worth everywhere you go.  ‍You stop handing your self-esteem to the opinions of others.
You begin to trust your own knowing.  ‍Because you become the source of the recognition you have always been seeking.
A Final Reflection
‍The next time you find yourself feeling unseen, pause for a moment and ask:
"What part of me am I not seeing?"
"What gift am I overlooking?"
"What truth about myself have I been waiting for somebody else to confirm?"
"What would change if I began acknowledging my own value today?"

The healing journey often begins when we stop asking the world to see our value and start recognising it ourselves.  Because when you truly see yourself, the opinions of others lose their power to define who you are.  And from that place, you can finally be seen without needing it.

Modern spirituality may refer to this accumulated suffering as the “pain body.”
But the pain body is far deeper than stored emotional pain alone.
It is the energetic residue of everything the nervous system, body, heart, and soul have not yet been able to fully process.
Every experience that overwhelms our capacity to fully feel, process, integrate, or safely express itself can leave an imprint within the system.

paras: "The female womb is not simply a place from which life emerges. It is a sacred threshold through which consciousness remembers its relationship with the infinite field of creative potential from which all life continually emerges."

blocks.html: For much of modern history, the female womb has been understood almost exclusively through the lens of biology. It is recognised as the organ through which new life is conceived, nourished and brought into the world. This understanding is both essential and profoundly important. Yet throughout history, the womb has also occupied another place within human consciousness. Across spiritual traditions, mystery schools and ancient cultures, it has been revered as a symbol of creation, transformation and the profound mystery from which life itself emerges. Although these traditions speak through different languages and symbols, they share a common intuition: before anything becomes visible, it first exists in an unseen state. Before birth there is gestation. Before expression there is potential. Humanity has repeatedly returned to the feminine as the keeper of this mystery.

Over many years as a Shamanic Practitioner, I have had the privilege of journeying alongside women from many different cultures and backgrounds. Although every healing journey is unique, certain patterns have revealed themselves with remarkable consistency. This blog is born from those observations, from my own personal journeying, and from a deep reverence for the spiritual intelligence of the womb. What follows is not presented as doctrine, nor as a universal truth that every woman must accept. It is the understanding that has gradually unfolded through direct experience, careful observation and years of accompanying women into the wisdom of their own womb space. I offer it as an invitation rather than a conclusion.

One of the most important lessons this work has taught me is that no two women journey in exactly the same way. While recurring themes often emerge, the symbolic language through which the womb communicates is deeply personal. One woman may encounter a lion, another an ancestor, another a river, another an ancient temple. One may experience silence where another encounters vivid imagery. None of these experiences are more correct than another because the spiritual intelligence of the womb communicates through the symbolic language each woman is most able to receive. For this reason, I do not ask anyone to recreate my experience. My hope is that by sharing the landscape that has gradually revealed itself to me, it may encourage you to enter your own inner landscape with greater curiosity, reverence and trust.

It was not always my understanding that the womb was a sacred threshold. Like many practitioners, my work initially centred on healing. The womb was a place where grief could be released, trauma witnessed, boundaries restored and feminine power reclaimed. These remain profoundly important aspects of the work, yet over time I began to sense that healing, while essential, was not the destination. Healing seemed to be preparing us for something deeper. It was clearing the ground for a relationship that extended beyond healing itself.

As my own relationship with the womb matured through years of journeying, a remarkable inner landscape gradually revealed itself. It was not something I consciously created, nor something I had studied beforehand. Rather, it unfolded naturally through repeated encounters that carried an unmistakable sense of coherence. The first presence I came to know was what I now call the Womb Guardian. She did not appear as an obstacle or a gatekeeper withholding access. Instead, she embodied discernment. Standing quietly at the threshold, she seemed to protect not only the womb itself, but the depth of encounter that lay beyond it. Over time I came to understand that her role was not to prevent entry, but to ensure that entry occurred through relationship rather than force.

Only when trust had been established did I find myself invited further inward. Beyond the Guardian I encountered another presence that gradually became known to me as the Inner Queen. She was not a queen in the worldly sense of power, status or authority over others. She represented something far quieter and infinitely more profound. She embodied sovereignty. In her presence there was no striving, no performance and no need to become anyone other than who I already was. She carried an unwavering sense of inner authority rooted not in control, but in truth. For a long time, I believed this was the destination of the journey.
Then something happened that fundamentally changed the way I understood the womb.

During one journey, while resting in the presence of the Inner Queen, the experience shifted in a way I had never anticipated. It did not feel as though I was leaving my body or escaping my womb. Instead, it felt as though the womb itself opened. Not physically, but consciously. The boundaries of my individual experience dissolved into a vastness that was impossible to measure. There were no walls, no edges and no sense of beginning or end. What I encountered was neither empty nor filled with symbolic imagery. It was alive with an indescribable sense of potential.

It felt as though every possibility that had ever existed, or could ever exist, rested within this immeasurable field before taking form. There was no urgency within it, no striving and no sense of becoming something else. There was only an extraordinary presence, an unmistakable intelligence and an infinite field of creative potential. It was profoundly familiar, not because I had consciously experienced it before, but because some deeper part of me recognised it. In that moment I did not feel that I had discovered something new. I felt that I had remembered something ancient.

Language has limits when describing experiences such as these. Any name we give them inevitably becomes smaller than the experience itself. Yet over the years I found myself continually returning to one phrase that most closely reflected what had been revealed. I came to understand this vastness as the Cosmic Womb. Not as another energetic organ. Not as a place somewhere beyond the stars. Nor as an energetic structure surrounding the physical body. Rather, I have come to understand the Cosmic Womb as the infinite field of creative potential from which all life continually emerges. The female womb did not create this field. Instead, the womb became the sacred threshold through which consciousness remembered its relationship with it.

That single journey transformed the way I understood healing. I no longer saw healing as the ultimate purpose of the womb. Healing became preparation. It became the gradual remembrance of everything that had been forgotten beneath layers of conditioning, protection and pain. The Womb Guardian was no longer simply protecting wounds; she was protecting the threshold. The Inner Queen was no longer simply teaching sovereignty; she was preparing consciousness for communion. The journey itself was no longer about collecting spiritual experiences or seeking extraordinary visions. It had become a journey of remembrance—a remembering of our relationship with the infinite field of creative potential from which all life continually emerges.

title: Best Healing Experiences in Ubud: A Curated Guide.
htmlTitle: Best Healing Experiences in Ubud: A Curated Guide. — Energy Healing Centre Ubud, Bali | The Juicy Effect
description: A curated insider's guide to the most meaningful healing experiences in Ubud, from shamanic energy work to womb healing, breathwork and Ayurveda.

excerptText: A curated insider's guide to the most meaningful healing experiences in Ubud, from shamanic energy work to womb healing, breathwork and Ayurveda.

blocks.html: Ubud has become a global pilgrimage site for women and men called to heal. The town's reputation is well earned. Tucked into the rice paddies and jungle of central Bali, Ubud offers a density and depth of wellbeing modalities that few places on earth can match. From ancient shamanic lineages and Balinese ceremony, to modern somatic therapies and breathwork, the breadth is genuinely overwhelming for a first time visitor.

This guide is for the traveller who has booked their flight and wants to spend their precious healing time on experiences that will actually move something, not the ones designed for the perfect photograph. We have curated it as practitioners working in Ubud since 2018, and we are mindful of one truth that has shaped how we work all these years.
The most powerful healing in Ubud is not always the loudest. The places that protect the work are often the ones doing it most deeply.
Below are the modalities most worth considering when you arrive, what to look for in a practitioner, and a few thoughts on how to choose what is right for the season you are in.
Why Ubud holds healing differently

Ubud's quality of healing is not an accident. The town sits inside a deeply spiritual culture. Balinese Hinduism weaves daily ceremony, offerings and reverence into the rhythm of ordinary life. You feel it on every street: the canang sari placed at thresholds, the temple bells at dawn, the slow politeness of people who live in real relationship with the unseen.

On top of this living lineage sits a layered community of practitioners, both Balinese and from around the world, many of whom have settled in Ubud for years to deepen their work. The natural geography helps: jungle on three sides, water everywhere, the volcanic energy of Mount Agung in the near distance. The pace is slower. The cost of unhurried time is lower than at home. All of this adds up to a container in which deep work is supported, not interrupted.
It also means there is a lot to choose from. Some of it is exquisite. Some of it is performative. The sections below help you tell the difference.
The healing experiences worth seeking out
blocks.text: The healing experiences worth seeking out

blocks.html: Shamanic energy healing

Shamanic energy healing is one of the oldest healing modalities on earth, found in lineages from Mongolia to the Andes to Bali itself. A session typically involves the practitioner working with subtle energy, drum, voice and altered states to clear stagnant patterns, retrieve lost soul fragments and restore the natural flow of life force in the body. It is not religious. It does not require you to believe anything. Most women who come for shamanic energy healing in Ubud arrive because something in them is asking for a deeper layer of release that talk based modalities have not reached.

Look for a practitioner with a recognised diploma or initiation, a steady presence, and a clear willingness to talk through what to expect before the session. The Juicy Effect offers shamanic energy healing as one of our core modalities. Sharon is a Certified Shamanic Practitioner with a Diploma from the Shaman College Circle of Earth and Spirit, and over fifteen years of experience holding this work.
Soul retrieval

Soul retrieval is a specific shamanic practice for calling back parts of ourselves that have been left behind during difficult or traumatic events. It is held with great care. The session usually weaves a guided journey, focused energy work, and integration support afterward. People often describe a feeling of coming home to themselves in the days that follow. It pairs beautifully with one or two other sessions across a stay rather than as a standalone, because the integration matters as much as the retrieval itself.
Hypnotherapy and inner child healing

Hypnotherapy is one of the most underrated modalities for travellers in Ubud, perhaps because it is less Instagrammable than ceremony work. It is also one of the most effective for shifting long held patterns. A skilled hypnotherapist works with the subconscious mind in a relaxed state to update old beliefs, release inner child wounds, and re-pattern responses you cannot reach through cognition alone. If you have done years of therapy and feel you understand your patterns intellectually but have not yet been able to shift them, hypnotherapy is often the missing layer. Look for a fully certified practitioner who works with a clear ethical frame.
Breathwork and trauma release

Breathwork in Ubud spans a wide spectrum. At one end is gentle conscious connected breathing for opening the chest and releasing stuck emotion. At the other is more intense holotropic style work that brings you into deep altered states. Both can be powerful. Both deserve a practitioner who knows how to slow you down, work with the nervous system, and pace the release so it lands in the body rather than overwhelming it. Trauma release breathwork is especially valuable for women carrying long held grief, anxiety or burnout. Avoid sessions that feel performative or where the facilitator is not present to you specifically.
Womb healing and feminine work

Womb healing has become one of the most sought after experiences in Ubud, and for good reason. The womb space holds far more than many of us were taught. Old relationship wounds, ancestral patterns, the imprint of unspoken truths, all live there. A skilled womb healing session, sometimes called yoni healing or sacred womb work, weaves energetic clearing, gentle somatic practice and ceremonial space. It is not sexual. It is not invasive. Done well, it returns women to a quality of sovereignty and inner authority that can feel revelatory. We hold this work both as a single Womb Healing session and as a deeper Womb Healing Immersion Package across several days. It is also the foundation of our online programme, Womb Alchemy, for women not yet able to come to Bali.
Sound healing and group ceremony

Sound baths, gong ceremonies and crystal bowl sessions are widely available in Ubud. They can be a beautiful entry point if you are new to energetic work, especially in a group format. They are excellent for nervous system regulation and softening the edges before going into deeper one to one work. As a general rule, group sound experiences open the field. Private sessions go into specific terrain. Many women find that a group ceremony in their first few days of Ubud helps them arrive more fully in the body, ready for whatever comes next.
Ayurveda and lifestyle medicine

Ayurveda is the five thousand year old Indian system of personalised medicine. In Ubud you will find Ayurvedic consultations, lifestyle plans, body therapies and food guidance, often woven into the daily life of practitioners working out of small clinics or larger wellness centres. An Ayurvedic consultation is one of the most useful things you can do early in your stay. It gives you a clear read of your current constitution and offers practical, daily rhythms to take home. The Juicy Effect offers Ayurvedic lifestyle consultations as both a single session and a longer Ayurvedic Lifestyle Package.
Vedic astrology and navigation work

Vedic astrology, also called Jyotish, is a precise system for understanding the timing and themes of your life. It is not about predicting the future. It is about meeting yourself within what is already happening. A Vedic astrology reading in Ubud is often a quiet, deeply grounding hour that gives you language for a chapter you are walking through. We offer Vedic astrology and a Medical Astrology variant that focuses specifically on body and health themes.
What to expect from a healing session in Ubud
blocks.text: What to expect from a healing session in Ubud

blocks.html: Most one to one sessions in Ubud last between 75 minutes and 2 hours. The price range is broad. A reputable single session at a centre with experienced practitioners typically sits between 80 USD and 250 USD. Anything significantly cheaper is worth looking at carefully, and anything significantly more expensive should be backed by serious credentials and a clear methodology, not just beautiful marketing.

On arrival you will usually be welcomed with water or tea, given a few minutes to land, and walked through what is about to happen. A good practitioner takes time to understand what you are bringing to the session before any work begins. You should never feel rushed, performed at, or pushed past your edges. The work should meet you where you are, and the integration after, often a few quiet minutes of journaling, water, perhaps a voice note from your practitioner the next day, is as important as the session itself.
If at any point a session feels off, you have every right to pause it. Trust your body's read of the practitioner. The good ones welcome that level of self trust in their clients.
How to choose what is right for you
blocks.text: How to choose what is right for you

blocks.html: A simple way to think about it. If you are arriving exhausted and on edge, start with a softer, body based modality. Sound healing, gentle breathwork, an Ayurvedic body treatment. Once your nervous system has settled, go deeper. Energy healing, hypnotherapy, womb work or soul retrieval will land more fully when you are not running on adrenaline.

If you have a specific situation you are working through, a relationship ending, a creative block, a pattern you cannot break, ask the practitioner directly which of their modalities best meets that. A good practitioner will tell you honestly if their work is not the right fit and refer you on.

If you have time, choose depth over volume. Three sessions over a week with one trusted practitioner usually does far more than six sessions across six different modalities. We see this every season. The women who walk away most changed are not the ones who tried everything.
Practical tips for healing in Ubud
blocks.text: Practical tips for healing in Ubud

items: Book your first session before you arrive, especially in high season. The most experienced practitioners are often booked weeks ahead.
Allow at least seven days in Ubud for any meaningful healing arc. Two weeks is better.
Stay close to your practitioner if you can. Ubud has good drivers, but reducing travel friction means you arrive at sessions softer.
Eat simply during your healing time. Local warung food and Ubud's beautiful plant based cafes both work. Your body integrates better without heavy or rich foods around sessions.
Avoid stacking too many ceremonies in a row. The deeper modalities need digestion time. A session most days is plenty.
Bring a journal. Some of the most important integration happens in the few days after a session, in writing.
Be gentle with yourself for at least 24 hours after deep work. Skip the late nights. Skip the cocktails. Drink water.
Ask for what you need. Practitioners would rather adjust the session than have you leave unsatisfied.

blocks.html: Where to begin

If this guide has resonated, we would love to welcome you. The Juicy Effect is a transformational wellbeing and healing centre based in Ubud, offering private sessions, multi day journeys and group workshops since 2018. Our team of four practitioners works across shamanic energy healing, hypnotherapy, breathwork, womb healing, Reiki, Ayurveda and Vedic astrology, with a deep commitment to holding the work safely, slowly and well.

Wherever you choose to begin your healing time in Ubud, our hope is that you find a practitioner whose presence steadies you. The work is sacred, the town is generous, and the timing is rarely an accident. If you feel called, trust it. Your body already knows.

Sharon Marie Keating is the founder of The Juicy Effect. She is a Certified Shamanic Practitioner, Hypnotherapist, Kinesiology Practitioner, Ayurvedic Lifestyle Consultant and Yoga Nidra Instructor with over fifteen years of experience. The challenge is that these questions rarely arrive with clear answers.  Many people assume they need a plan.
What they often need first is clarity.
Why Clarity Matters
When people feel uncertain, the natural tendency is to seek solutions immediately.
But action taken without clarity often creates more confusion rather than less.
The most effective decisions are usually built upon a deeper understanding of what is actually happening beneath the surface.

For many people, particularly professionals, executives, and business owners, this formula works remarkably well. Promotions arrive. Businesses grow. Financial pressure reduces. Opportunities increase.
Yet something unexpected often happens.
The achievement that was supposed to bring lasting fulfilment doesn't quite deliver.

This can be confusing because from the outside, life appears successful. Friends may admire your career. Colleagues may respect your accomplishments. Family members may see stability and security. But internally, questions begin to emerge":

items: Is this what I want to keep doing for the next ten years?
Why do I feel restless when everything is going well?
Why does another promotion feel less exciting than it once did?

blocks.html: The problem is not that success is bad. Success solves many problems. Financial stress, uncertainty, and lack of opportunity are real challenges.

The problem is that success and fulfilment are not the same thing.  Success is often measured externally. Fulfilment is experienced internally.  Success can be seen by others. Fulfilment can only be felt by you.
Many people spend decades pursuing achievement without ever stopping to ask a different question: What actually gives me energy?
This question becomes increasingly important in midlife.

At twenty-five, building skills and proving yourself may be the priority. At fifty-five, the calculation changes. Time becomes more valuable than status. Meaning becomes more important than recognition. Experiences often matter more than possessions.
This does not mean abandoning ambition. It means redefining it.
Some people discover fulfilment through mentoring others. Some through creating businesses. Some through travel, learning, community involvement, or entirely new careers.
The answer is different for everyone.

What matters is recognising that fulfilment rarely arrives automatically as a reward for success. It requires its own attention, reflection, and intentional design.  Many people spend years building a successful life.  Far fewer spend time deciding what that life is ultimately for.
Perhaps the most important question is not whether you have been successful.
Perhaps it is whether the life you have built still feels like one you want to keep living.

blocks.html: If you are searching for the best healers in Ubud, you are probably looking for more than a relaxing treatment. You may be looking for clarity, emotional release, energetic balance, spiritual guidance, or simply a safe space to reconnect with yourself.

Ubud has become one of the most well-known places in Bali for healing, wellness, yoga, meditation, energy work, and personal transformation. But with so many options available, it can be difficult to know where to begin.

Should you visit a traditional Balinese healer? Book an energy healing session? Try chakra healing, breathwork, hypnotherapy, sound healing, or a private retreat? And how do you know which healer is right for you?

The truth is, the “best healer in Ubud” is not always the most famous person or the one with the biggest online following. The best healer is the one who feels safe, grounded, experienced, ethical, and aligned with what you are genuinely seeking.

This guide will help you understand the different types of healers in Ubud, what to look for, what to avoid, and how to choose a healing experience that supports real personal insight rather than unrealistic promises.
Why People Come to Ubud for Healing
blocks.text: Why People Come to Ubud for Healing

blocks.html: Many people come to Ubud because they are going through a turning point.

Some are recovering from burnout. Some are navigating grief, heartbreak, stress, anxiety, or major life change. Others feel disconnected from themselves and want to explore a deeper spiritual path. best healers in Ubud
energy healer Ubud
spiritual healer Ubud Bali
Balinese healer Ubud
chakra healing Ubud
sound healing Ubud
emotional healing Bali
private healing session Ubud

healing centre in Ubud
